Sam (Docs): Opening a tiny coordination thread: PR to add a "Terraform module outputs" appendix for Dedicated provisioning + sample SLA alerting rules. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2777
Priya (SRE): Nice. We need concrete output names so monitoring dashboards can autosync. Suggest outputs: `pool_id`, `pool_tier`, `pool_sla_label`, and `pool_node_count`.
Hector (Infra): Also include an output for `tenant_isolation_annotation` (some customer infra still reads `isolation_level` from old modules). Add a migration note mapping `isolation_level` -> `tenant_isolation_annotation`.
Sam (Docs): I'll add a small migration table. Good call on names.
Lin (SDK): Heads up: the Go SDK sample in the new appendix currently uses `MaxBatch` and `BatchSize` in different places. Our canonical param is `batch_limit` across SDKs. Can we standardize the example to use `batch_limit`?
Sam (Docs): Yep, will normalize. Also planning to include a runnable Prometheus alert example for SLA breach (evictions > 0 or sustained 5m p95 latency > threshold).
Priya (SRE): Alert idea: two rules: (1) Eviction spike: sum(rate(dedicated_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool) > 0 -> page on-call. (2) SLA latency breach: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(dedicated_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) > <pool_threshold>. Add runbook links.
Sam (Docs): Adding both rules and linking to /runbooks/dedicated-sla. Also adding a small Terraform outputs snippet: 
```hcl
output "pool_id" {
  value = module.dedicated.pool_id
}
output "pool_tier" {
  value = module.dedicated.tier
}
output "pool_sla_label" {
  value = module.dedicated.sla_label
}
output "tenant_isolation_annotation" {
  value = module.dedicated.tenant_isolation_annotation
}
```
Hector (Infra): For the migration note, add this mapping: `isolation_level` -> `tenant_isolation_annotation` and `replica_min` -> `min_replicas`. Lots of older examples still copy the old names.
Lin (SDK): Adding a Go snippet suggestion for the appendix. Use the public client and `batch_limit` param: 
```go
package main
import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  redwood "github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go"
)
func main() {
  client := redwood.NewClient()
  resp, err := client.Generate(context.Background(), redwood.GenerateParams{
    Model: "redwood-dedicated-1",
    Prompt: "Hello",
    BatchLimit: 4, // canonical param name in Go bindings
  })
  if err != nil {
    panic(err)
  }
  fmt.Println(resp.Text)
}
```
Sam (Docs): Thanks Lin — I'll include that. Note: doc text will call out that the Go SDK uses `BatchLimit` (camel case) while Python/JS use `batch_limit`.
Priya (SRE): Also include an example alert config in YAML for PagerDuty/Slack integration and a short troubleshooting section: "If alerts fire during scale events, check scale_down_cooldown and drain_timeout to avoid noisy false positives."
Sam (Docs): Added alert YAML snippet and the troubleshooting note. Also fixed an internal broken link CI flagged: `/internal/observability/metrics` -> should be `/observability/metrics`.

Sam (Docs): Added relabel config snippet and a tiny note recommending `default_batch_limit` var for tiny on-prem pools (`default_batch_limit = 3`).
Lin (SDK): Can we file a follow-up to enroll the new Go snippet in docs-smoke? We want to avoid param regressions across languages.
